subject: sst
prompt_en: Why is the soil of the Northern Plains so good for farming?
prompt_hi: Uttari maidanon (Northern Plains) ki mitti kheti ke liye itni achhi kyun hai?
answer: It is alluvial soil: fine, fertile soil carried down from the Himalayas and spread by rivers like the Ganga, Yamuna and Brahmaputra.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why do the Ganga and Yamuna have water all year, while many Deccan rivers become thin in summer?
prompt_hi: Ganga aur Yamuna mein saal bhar paani kyun rehta hai, jabki Deccan ki kai nadiyaan garmi mein patli ho jaati hain?
answer: Himalayan rivers are fed by melting snow and glaciers as well as rain, so they flow all year; most Deccan rivers depend only on monsoon rain.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: what would happen to farms and towns in the Northern Plains if many Himalayan glaciers shrank a lot?
prompt_hi: Socho: agar Himalaya ke bahut saare glacier bahut chhote ho jaayein, toh Northern Plains ke kheton aur shehron ka kya hoga?
answer: Rivers would carry less water in the dry months, so there would be less water for irrigation and drinking, and crops and towns would suffer.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Many traditional houses in the Thar have thick mud walls and small windows. Why?
prompt_hi: Thar ke bahut se purane gharon ki deewarein mitti ki moti aur khidkiyaan chhoti hoti hain. Kyun?
answer: Thick mud walls and small windows keep out the strong daytime heat and hot sandy winds, and keep the house warmer during cold desert nights.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Someone says the Thar Desert is empty and nothing can live there. Give three examples that show people, animals and plants do live there, and how they manage with little water.
prompt_hi: Koi kehta hai ki Thar registaan khaali hai aur wahan kuch nahi reh sakta. 3 example do jo dikhayein ki wahan log, jaanwar aur paudhe rehte hain, aur kam paani mein kaise guzaara karte hain.
answer: People live in villages and towns (like Jaisalmer and Barmer), store rainwater in underground tanks (tankas) and grow hardy crops like bajra; camels can go many days without water; khejri trees have deep roots and give fodder and shade.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare life in a village in Ladakh with life in a village in the Ganga plains: one difference each in crops, houses and travel.
prompt_hi: Ladakh ke ek gaon aur Ganga ke maidan ke ek gaon ki zindagi compare karo: fasal, ghar aur safar mein ek-ek fark batao.
answer: Ladakh: cold, dry, high — barley and apricots, short growing season; flat-roofed stone or mud-brick houses with thick walls; mountain roads and passes closed by snow in winter. Ganga plains: hot summers, fertile flat land — rice, wheat, sugarcane; brick houses, often sloping roofs; easy flat roads and railways.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Think about your own town or village. Which physical region is it in? Give two ways the land or rivers there shape what people grow, eat or do for work.
prompt_hi: Apne shehar ya gaon ke baare mein socho. Woh kis physical region mein hai? Do tareeke batao jinse wahan ki zameen ya nadiyaan logon ki kheti, khaana ya kaam-dhandha tay karti hain.
answer: A correct answer names the right region for the child's place and gives two real links between landform/rivers and life (e.g. coastal town → fishing and coconut; plains → wheat and rice farming; plateau → cotton on black soil; hills → terrace farming, tea).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistakes: "The Deccan Plateau is a young mountain range made of soft soil brought by rivers, and its big rivers all flow west."
prompt_hi: Galti dhoondho: "Deccan Pathaar ek nayi parvat shrinkhla hai jo nadiyon ki laayi naram mitti se bani hai, aur iski saari badi nadiyaan pashchim ki taraf behti hain."
answer: The Deccan is an old plateau of hard rock (not a young mountain range of soft river soil); most of its big rivers (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi) flow east into the Bay of Bengal — only a few, like the Narmada and Tapi, flow west.

subject: sst
prompt_en: On a physical map, one line of hills runs unbroken close to the west coast; another runs broken into pieces along the east. Name each and say why the eastern one is broken.
prompt_hi: Physical map par ek pahadiyon ki line pashchimi tat ke paas bina toote chalti hai; doosri poorab mein tukdon mein bati hai. Dono ke naam batao aur poorvi wali tooti kyun hai?
answer: The unbroken western line is the Western Ghats (Sahyadri); the broken eastern line is the Eastern Ghats, cut through by big east-flowing rivers like the Godavari, Krishna, Mahanadi and Kaveri.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a cousin from another country why India is called a land of geographical diversity. Use at least three regions and say how life differs in each.
prompt_hi: Videsh mein rehne wale apne cousin ko samjhao ki India ko bhaugolik vividhta (geographical diversity) wala desh kyun kehte hain. Kam se kam 3 regions lo aur batao wahan zindagi kaise alag hai.
answer: Key idea: India has mountains, plains, desert, plateau, coasts and islands side by side; each has different height, soil, rivers and climate, which leads to different crops, homes, food and work.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why do so many people live in the Northern Plains?
prompt_hi: Northern Plains mein itne saare log kyun rehte hain?
answer: The land is flat and fertile with rivers that flow all year, so farming is easy and food is plentiful; flat land also makes roads, railways, towns and trade easy.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A trekker starts at Dehradun (about 650 m high) and climbs to a pass about 4,000 m high. Predict: will it get warmer or colder as she climbs? Why?
prompt_hi: Ek trekker Dehradun (lagbhag 650 m) se chal ke lagbhag 4,000 m oonche darre tak chadhti hai. Socho: oopar jaate hue thand badhegi ya garmi? Kyun?
answer: Colder: air temperature falls as height increases (roughly 6 °C for every 1,000 m), so at 4,000 m it is much colder even though she is "closer to the sun".

subject: sst
prompt_en: Sort these into weather or climate: (a) It is raining in Pune right now. (b) Rajasthan is dry most of the year. (c) Puri will be windy tomorrow. (d) Shillong has cool summers.
prompt_hi: Inko weather ya climate mein baanto: (a) Pune mein abhi baarish ho rahi hai. (b) Rajasthan saal ke zyaadatar samay sookha rehta hai. (c) Kal Puri mein tez hawa chalegi. (d) Shillong ki garmiyaan thandi hoti hain.
answer: Weather: (a) and (c). Climate: (b) and (d).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Match each instrument to what it measures: thermometer, barometer, anemometer, wind vane, rain gauge, hygrometer.
prompt_hi: Har instrument ko uske naap se milao: thermometer, barometer, anemometer, wind vane, rain gauge, hygrometer.
answer: Thermometer – temperature; barometer – air pressure; anemometer – wind speed; wind vane – wind direction; rain gauge – rainfall; hygrometer – humidity.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistakes: "Ravi measured wind speed with a wind vane and rainfall with a thermometer."
prompt_hi: Galti pakdo: "Ravi ne hawa ki speed wind vane se naapi aur baarish thermometer se."
answer: Wind speed is measured with an anemometer (a wind vane shows direction), and rainfall with a rain gauge (a thermometer measures temperature).

subject: sst
prompt_en: On a sunny afternoon at the beach, a cool breeze blows from the sea onto the land. Explain why.
prompt_hi: Dhoop wali dopahar ko beach par samundar se zameen ki taraf thandi hawa chalti hai. Kyun?
answer: Land heats up faster than water; warm air over the land rises, creating lower pressure there; cooler, higher-pressure air over the sea moves in to replace it — the sea breeze.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Now predict: at night, which way will the breeze blow at the same beach? Why?
prompt_hi: Ab socho: raat ko usi beach par hawa kis taraf chalegi? Kyun?
answer: From the land to the sea (a land breeze), because land cools faster than water at night, so the air over the sea is warmer and rises, making lower pressure over the sea.

subject: sst
prompt_en: There are no trees in the middle of the sea, yet strong winds blow there. What does this tell you about what causes wind?
prompt_hi: Beech samundar mein ek bhi ped nahi hota, phir bhi wahan tez hawa chalti hai. Isse hawa ke kaaran ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
answer: Trees do not make wind; wind is air moving from areas of high pressure to areas of low pressure, caused by uneven heating by the sun.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Tomorrow's forecast card says: Max 38 °C, Min 27 °C, humidity 80%, wind from the south-west at 20 km/h, chance of rain 70%. Say in words what tomorrow will feel like and what you should carry.
prompt_hi: Kal ke forecast card par likha hai: Max 38 °C, Min 27 °C, humidity 80%, hawa dakshin-pashchim se 20 km/h, baarish ki sambhavna 70%. Shabdon mein batao kal kaisa lagega aur kya saath le jaana chahiye.
answer: A hot, sticky (humid) day with a steady breeze from the south-west and a good chance of rain — carry water and an umbrella or raincoat, and wear light clothes.

subject: sst
prompt_en: IMD has issued an orange alert for heavy rain in your district. What does an orange alert mean, and what should your family do?
prompt_hi: IMD ne aapke zile ke liye heavy rain ka orange alert diya hai. Orange alert ka matlab kya hai, aur aapke parivaar ko kya karna chahiye?
answer: Orange means "be prepared": severe weather is likely. Keep updated, avoid unnecessary travel, keep torch, water and phone charged, stay away from flooded roads and rivers, and follow official advice. (Green = no warning, yellow = be aware, red = take action.)

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare a December morning in Delhi with a December morning in Chennai: temperature and humidity.
prompt_hi: December ki ek subah Delhi aur Chennai mein compare karo: taapmaan (temperature) aur humidity.
answer: Delhi: cold (often below 10 °C) and often foggy at dawn; the cold air holds much less water vapour overall. Chennai: mild and warm (around 20–25 °C) with much more water vapour in the air (more humid), because it is near the sea and closer to the equator; Chennai may even get rain from the north-east monsoon in December.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Plan a one-week weather diary for your home. Which three weather elements could you measure with simple things, and how would you measure each?
prompt_hi: Ghar ke liye ek hafte ki weather diary plan karo. Kaun se 3 element tum seedhi-saadi cheezon se naap sakte ho, aur har ek kaise naapoge?
answer: For example: temperature with a thermometer at the same time each day; rainfall by collecting rain in a straight-sided bottle and measuring the depth in mm with a ruler; wind direction with a ribbon or paper vane and a compass; cloud cover by looking at the sky. Record at the same time and place each day.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a younger child the difference between weather and climate using the clothes in your cupboard.
prompt_hi: Apne cupboard ke kapdon ka example le kar chhote bachche ko weather aur climate ka fark samjhao.
answer: Key idea: what you choose to wear today depends on the weather (short-term); which clothes your family owns at all — many sweaters or mostly cotton — depends on the climate (long-term pattern).

subject: sst
prompt_en: A bottle rain gauge collected 12 mm of rain on Monday and 30 mm on Tuesday. How much rain fell in the two days, and which instrument idea is this?
prompt_hi: Bottle wale rain gauge mein Monday ko 12 mm aur Tuesday ko 30 mm baarish jama hui. Do din mein kitni baarish hui, aur yeh kaunse instrument ka idea hai?
answer: 42 mm of rain in total; this is a rain gauge, which measures rainfall as the depth of water in millimetres.

subject: sst
prompt_en: On a sticky, sweaty afternoon in Kolkata it has not rained at all. Explain the difference between humidity and rainfall using this day.
prompt_hi: Kolkata mein ek chipchipi, paseene wali dopahar ko bilkul baarish nahi hui. Is din ka example le kar humidity aur rainfall ka fark samjhao.
answer: Humidity is the amount of invisible water vapour in the air — high humidity makes us feel sticky because sweat dries slowly; rainfall is water actually falling from clouds as drops. A day can be very humid with no rain at all.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why is the difference between summer and winter temperatures much smaller in Mumbai than in Delhi?
prompt_hi: Mumbai mein garmi aur sardi ke taapmaan ka fark Delhi se kaafi kam kyun hota hai?
answer: Mumbai is on the coast, and the sea heats and cools slowly, keeping it mild all year; Delhi is far inland, so it gets very hot summers and cold winters (an extreme climate).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Put these monsoon steps in order: (a) moist winds blow in from the Indian Ocean; (b) the land heats up strongly in summer; (c) winds rise over the Western Ghats, cool and drop rain; (d) low pressure forms over north-west India.
prompt_hi: Monsoon ke in steps ko sahi kram mein lagao: (a) Hind Mahasagar se nam hawayein aati hain; (b) garmi mein zameen bahut garam hoti hai; (c) hawayein Pashchimi Ghat par chadh ke thandi hoti hain aur baarish girati hain; (d) uttar-pashchim India par low pressure banta hai.
answer: b → d → a → c

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why is Mawsynram in Meghalaya one of the wettest places on Earth, while Jaisalmer in Rajasthan is very dry?
prompt_hi: Meghalaya ka Mawsynram duniya ki sabse geeli jagahon mein se ek kyun hai, jabki Rajasthan ka Jaisalmer itna sookha kyun?
answer: Moist monsoon winds from the Bay of Bengal are funnelled into the Khasi hills and forced to rise steeply over Mawsynram, so they cool and drop huge amounts of rain. Jaisalmer is far west in the Thar; the winds reaching it carry little moisture and are not forced to rise (the Aravallis lie along the wind's path, not across it), so little rain falls.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if the Western Ghats did not exist, how would rainfall on the Konkan coast and in the interior of Maharashtra change?
prompt_hi: Socho: agar Pashchimi Ghat hota hi nahi, toh Konkan tat aur Maharashtra ke andar ke ilaakon mein baarish kaise badalti?
answer: The Konkan coast would get much less rain, because the winds would not be forced up to cool and drop their moisture; the interior would no longer be in such a strong rain shadow, so rain would be spread more evenly between the coast and the interior.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistakes: "In winter the sea becomes hotter than the land, so moist winds from the sea bring the south-west monsoon to Kerala in December."
prompt_hi: Galti dhoondho: "Sardi mein samundar zameen se zyada garam ho jaata hai, isliye samundar ki nam hawayein December mein Kerala mein south-west monsoon laati hain."
answer: The south-west monsoon comes in summer (it reaches Kerala around the start of June), when the LAND is hotter than the sea. In winter the land is cooler and winds blow from land to sea (north-east); that retreating monsoon brings rain mainly to the Tamil Nadu coast.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A rainfall chart for a city shows little rain from June to September but heavy rain from October to December. Which part of India is it probably in, and why?
prompt_hi: Ek shehar ke rainfall chart mein June-September mein kam baarish aur October-December mein bahut baarish dikhti hai. Yeh shayad India ke kis hisse mein hai, aur kyun?
answer: Probably on the Tamil Nadu (Coromandel) coast, e.g. Chennai: it lies in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats during the south-west monsoon, and gets most rain from the retreating (north-east) monsoon in October–December.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare the climates of Leh (Ladakh) and Thiruvananthapuram (Kerala), and give one way homes differ.
prompt_hi: Leh (Ladakh) aur Thiruvananthapuram (Kerala) ki jalvaayu compare karo, aur gharon mein ek fark batao.
answer: Leh: very high, cold and dry, freezing winters, very little rain — thick walls, flat roofs, small windows to keep warm. Thiruvananthapuram: low, coastal, warm and humid all year, heavy monsoon rain — sloping roofs to shed rain, open, airy houses.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why do farmers in much of India wait for the monsoon before sowing rice?
prompt_hi: India ke kai hisson mein kisaan dhaan (rice) bone se pehle monsoon ka intezaar kyun karte hain?
answer: Rice needs a lot of water, and in many areas monsoon rain is the main source of water for the fields (kharif season).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Describe your own town's climate across the year: the hottest months, the rainiest months, and one festival or food that fits a season.
prompt_hi: Apne shehar ki saal bhar ki jalvaayu batao: sabse garam mahine, sabse zyada baarish wale mahine, aur ek tyohaar ya khaana jo kisi mausam se juda ho.
answer: A correct answer matches the child's region (e.g. north India: hottest April–June, rain July–September, winter December–January) and links a festival or food to a season (e.g. Makar Sankranti or Pongal with harvest, mangoes in summer, hot pakoras in the rains).

subject: sst
prompt_en: How is climate change affecting India? Give two effects and one thing families or schools can do.
prompt_hi: Climate change India ko kaise prabhaavit kar raha hai? Do asar batao aur ek cheez jo parivaar ya school kar sakte hain.
answer: Effects: more frequent heatwaves, very heavy rain and floods in short bursts, an erratic monsoon that hurts farming, and shrinking Himalayan glaciers. Actions: save electricity and water, plant and protect trees, use public transport or cycles, reduce waste.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Two towns are at the same latitude: one on the coast at sea level, one in the hills at 2,000 m. Predict which is cooler in summer and why.
prompt_hi: Do shehar ek hi latitude par hain: ek samundar kinare (sea level par), ek pahadon mein 2,000 m oonchai par. Garmi mein kaun zyada thanda hoga aur kyun?
answer: The hill town at 2,000 m is cooler, because temperature falls as altitude increases.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a friend how the monsoon works, using the idea of beach sand and sea water on a hot day.
prompt_hi: Garam din par beach ki ret aur samundar ke paani ka example le kar dost ko samjhao ki monsoon kaise kaam karta hai.
answer: Key idea: land (like sand) heats faster than the sea; hot air over the land rises and creates low pressure; moist winds from the sea blow in; when they rise over hills they cool and rain falls; in winter the pattern reverses.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Put these in order from earliest to latest: Mahajanapadas emerge (c. 600 BCE); Constitution of India comes into force (1950 CE); Harappan cities at their height (c. 2600 BCE); Chandragupta Maurya founds an empire (c. 321 BCE).
prompt_hi: Inko sabse pehle se sabse baad ke kram mein lagao: Mahajanapada ubharte hain (lagbhag 600 BCE); Bharat ka Samvidhan laagu hota hai (1950 CE); Harappa ke shehar charam par (lagbhag 2600 BCE); Chandragupta Maurya samrajya banate hain (lagbhag 321 BCE).
answer: Harappan cities (c. 2600 BCE) → Mahajanapadas (c. 600 BCE) → Chandragupta Maurya (c. 321 BCE) → Constitution (1950 CE).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistake: "Rajagriha's wall was built in 500 BCE, so it is older than a coin made in 600 BCE."
prompt_hi: Galti pakdo: "Rajagriha ki deewar 500 BCE mein bani, isliye woh 600 BCE mein bane sikke se purani hai."
answer: Wrong way round: 600 BCE is earlier than 500 BCE, so the 600 BCE coin would be about 100 years older than the 500 BCE wall.

subject: sst
prompt_en: What does the word "janapada" mean?
prompt_hi: "Janapada" shabd ka matlab kya hai?
answer: The land where a jana (a people or clan) set foot and settled.
